migration.description: Bound artifact content recovery selection to an ordered partial index.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one artifact recovery follow-up; an online retryable index keeps recurring content and final-object reconciliation bounded as artifact history grows.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The migration adds only an internal PostgreSQL lookup index. It does not change REST or MCP shapes, row values, or the fail-closed behavior of earlier candidates; the recovery-capable candidate uses the index when selecting existing content and final-object recheck rows.

durable_state.description: conversation_artifacts content-recovery work is selected by staging_reclaim_after, created_at and id through a partial index restricted to unavailable content-mismatch and final-object recheck rows.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL partial B-tree index managed by embedded Goose migration 00016 outside a transaction with a dedicated migration session, a session-local current_schema() search_path, and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY; no table, column, or historical data rewrite is performed, and a failed attempt is dropped and retried without resolving an index through another schema.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Phase-one artifact content-recovery candidate containing migration 00015.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one artifact content-recovery candidate containing migration 00016.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Earlier candidates ignore the additive index and continue to read the existing artifact rows fail-closed; the recovery-capable candidate benefits from bounded selection after 00016 commits.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Replace any incomplete current-schema attempt and create a partial lookup index for due unavailable content-mismatch or final-object recheck rows with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction, without rewriting historical artifact values or resolving an index from another schema.

progress_signals: The non-transactional concurrent build keeps ordinary artifact writes available; Goose records migration 00016 only after the complete index build succeeds.
Recovery selection remains ordered by due time and bounded by the existing limit while PostgreSQL can use the partial index for content and final-object recheck rows.
pause_points: If a concurrent build is canceled or times out, the next migration attempt drops only the current-schema index and retries before enabling the recurring recovery loop.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version; the index may remain in place while content-mismatch recovery admission is disabled

required_test_evidence: Migration from 00015 creates the partial index without a transaction, repeated migration is idempotent, and a rolled-back and re-entered attempt is recoverable.
The shared application pool retains its configured search_path after migration; migration-only session settings are not reused by application queries.
The pg_indexes definition and EXPLAIN plan show the partial index matches the content and final-object recovery predicate and ordered limit.
Recovery selection returns due content and final-object recheck rows in bounded order without changing row values or states.
